entries.capability_summary: diaktoros (community, maintained by coe0718) Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files you provide; edits Hermes's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose, and restore writes one back into the Hermes home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Hermes home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices to the chat you name; deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: doc-markdown (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Convert one local file to Markdown with doc_convert on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — the doc_markdown toolset is on by default on every surface, including a gateway, so anyone you allow there can call doc_convert; stop it with hermes tools. It does not fetch pages. Unattended sessions still convert when Hermes calls the tool. This plugin creates no cron job. A child process runs MarkItDown with no Hermes keys in its environment; on macOS the plugin runs ps about every 10 ms to watch that child's memory. It stops 8 seconds after its converters load, at 60 seconds if loading never finishes, or above 922746880 bytes. It is not a sandbox: after realpath it may read any allowlisted path it can open. Unpublished Hermes code locates the Hermes home, and a failed check refuses the path. Removal deletes the plugin directory, not the markitdown package. Windows was not tested. entries.capability_summary: entropicmem (community, maintained by Ufonik88) Durable local memory for Hermes agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under HERMES_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to HERMES_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to HERMES_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default. This plugin registers tool(s): entropicmem_remember, entropicmem_recall, entropicmem_query, entropicmem_patch_core, entropicmem_stats, entropicmem_get, entropicmem_consolidate; hook(s): on_memory_write, on_session_switch, on_session_end, on_turn_start, on_pre_compress. entries.capability_summary: evalroute (community, maintained by keppy) Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "hermes evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run hermes -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into HERMES_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "hermes evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query hermes chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except HERMES_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "hermes evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "hermes evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.9.2,<0.10), declared as a Python dependency that Hermes installs on your confirmation. This plugin registers tool(s): evalroute_route; hook(s): pre_llm_call, pre_command, post_llm_call. Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: event-read (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar. This plugin registers tool(s): list_events, read_event; requires env var(s): CALDAV_URL, CALDAV_USER, CALDAV_PASSWORD. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: fish-audio (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) The official Fish Audio plugin, maintained by Electric Sheep: expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Hermes Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Hermes speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and live dictation captions on Hermes 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices and fish_transcribe tools, /fish and hermes fish commands, and three skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to api.fish.audio's realtime speech-to-text endpoint while you speak, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model, whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Hermes stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Hermes's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and Hermes config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Hermes's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. entries.capability_summary: fleet-policy (community, maintained by Julientalbot) For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`hermes fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). This plugin hook(s): pre_api_request, pre_auxiliary_call; middleware: llm_execution. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: gbrain-pointer (community, maintained by praggybuilds) Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry. This plugin requires env var(s): GBRAIN_MCP_CLIENT_ID, GBRAIN_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

heartbeat2 (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) Wakes and watchers for Hermes agents, maintained by Electric Sheep. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or Hermes event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions). A wake is a turn in the same messaging DM that armed it, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Watchers decide without a model call; the agent answers each wake with a structured verdict (notify or stay silent, never a typed sentinel); a no-op governor slows, then pauses pointless wakes and asks once. Every guardrail is a user setting (quiet hours, daily caps, unanswered mute, floors, lifetimes) that the agent works inside and can never widen. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps; HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire, and a wake that could never fire before it expires is refused. v0.1 delivers to messaging-gateway DMs only and needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow_gateway_injection: true. Disclosure — wakes and watchers run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes and watchers itself unless you set agent_can_create to ask_first or no; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote ` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Hermes blocks from reading; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry. This plugin registers tool(s): pulse; hook(s): pre_gateway_dispatch, gateway_platform_event, pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, post_api_request, transform_llm_output, on_session_end, agent_loop_stopped, on_session_reset, kanban_task_completed, kanban_task_blocked, on_kanban_worker_exited, subagent_stop, api_request_error. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. .tool_progress is off (quiet injection requested upstream: NousResearch/hermes-agent#136825).; v0.1 delivers only to messaging-gateway DMs; CLI, TUI, Desktop, API-server and cron arming are refused until Hermes core supports silent injected turns there.; When Hermes falls back to another model during a wake turn, its model-fallback notice is posted to the chat, even for a wake that stays silent (NousResearch/hermes-agent#137738)..

entries.capability_summary: hermes-call-ledger (community, maintained by skappafrost) Per-call cost ledger for Hermes Desktop: every model call Hermes makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by Hermes' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO_PAT read through Hermes's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from hermes-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT). This plugin hook(s): post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error; requires env var(s): VILAO_PAT. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-cloud-file-manager (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) Cloud Files for Hermes Desktop — browse, search, create folders and bulk-upload files and whole folders to the machine your agent runs on, read and edit its Markdown and text files (view first; nothing is written until you review the line diff and press Save), import files from the agent's own Google Drive, and hand the agent file locations from the chat + menu without re-uploading. Built for remote gateways (token or sign-in); works locally too. Disclosure — adds a file API to the gateway (dashboard plugin routes under the gateway's existing auth) over the agent's working folders, by default terminal.cwd or else the gateway user's home with its dot-entries hidden. It lists and searches those folders, reads Markdown and text files, creates folders and writes uploads and Drive imports (staged as hidden .cfm-* temp files in the destination folder; a name clash keeps both files). It overwrites only an existing .md/.markdown/.txt file you open and explicitly Save in its editor (refused if the file changed since you opened it). It never deletes your files (it removes only its own stale or aborted .cfm-* temp files and staging folders), never follows links out of those folders, and never lists, reads or writes the agent's Hermes home apart from a working folder set inside it (roots, terminal.cwd, or a workspace/ folder it creates when the working folder would be the home itself). Its only network use is Google Drive, read-only, through the agent's own google-workspace skill, whose scripts (from skills/productivity/google-workspace in the agent's Hermes home, else the copy bundled with Hermes) it runs with the gateway's Python and a minimal environment without API keys; the plugin never reads the Google token. While Desktop is open it re-checks Drive sign-in about once a minute; otherwise it makes no network calls. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-dreaming (community, maintained by itpartypattaya) Nightly deterministic memory consolidation ("dreaming"): corroborates candidate facts with what humans actually said on distinct days, proposes the few worth keeping with a verbatim edit anchor, asks whether stale memory entries still hold, and wakes the agent only when there is work — including a memory file close to its char limit. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — scripts make no network or LLM calls and open state.db and every fact store read-only (SQLite mode=ro); they also read Hermes config.yaml's memory/timezone keys and the holographic plugin's db_path/scope/cron_writes/min_trust_threshold (the floor recall applies, so a rejected fact is only reported when the store still trusts it) and, to say so in install.py --check, embeddings/mirror_memory_writes, the pending/memory approval queue, cron/jobs.json (to find their own jobs) and — only when chat_stores is set, with holographic scope user/chat/thread — the per-chat databases next to the store (counts of every one; facts of the chats listed in promote_from). The user-run installer copies three gate scripts into $HERMES_HOME/scripts, seeds $HERMES_HOME/dreaming.json and, through Hermes' cron Python API, creates (or with --rebind re-points) two agent cron jobs bound to this plugin's own skill with only the memory toolset, plus one no_agent job (every 15 min, no model) that reads the fact stores to keep a hash index of diary lines and, for facts holographic >= 0.8.0 has forgotten, rewrites the dream's own cache files and diary without them and deletes the output files of the dream's own cron jobs that mention them (by id or verbatim text); with a chat --deliver target the reports are attached as a session you can reply to. The agent runs send recent human messages (up to 200 / 40k chars, each with its chat type and sender id) and fact snippets to your configured model; state goes to $HERMES_HOME/cache and a diary to $HERMES_HOME/memories/DREAMS.md (configurable); memory files are changed by the agent only through the regular memory tool, and with the holographic provider it also adds candidate facts via fact_store (with holographic >= 0.8.0 also change / end / correct / forget, the last three only on a human's own answer; forget is irreversible), lowers trust on human-rejected facts via fact_feedback, with holographic >= 0.15.0 raises trust (fact_feedback confirmed, +0.05, at most 10 facts a night) on facts people repeated on two or more different days and, when keywords.enabled is set (off by default), adds search keywords to facts via fact_store update. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.0.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-experientiallabs (community, maintained by kyoto-aircon) Experiential Labs - OpenAI-compatible multi-model gateway provider (chat, /model picker, aux and curated fallback models, /usage wallet snapshot). All network calls go to api.experientiallabs.ai - /v1 chat + models via Hermes' own transport, /api/v1/credits and /api/v1/key only when /usage runs; no telemetry; credentials resolve through Hermes routes (hermes auth / .env). Disclosure — When you pick Experiential Labs as your model, every prompt, tool result and attachment of that session goes to api.experientiallabs.ai, a third-party gateway that routes to upstream model vendors. /usage sends your key to its Cost API (GET /credits and /key) or to the cost_api_base you set. Independent integration, not affiliated with Experiential Labs. This plugin requires env var(s): EXPLABS_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-field-notes (community, maintained by itpartypattaya) Field notes for a Hermes install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each hermes update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.21.6. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the Hermes core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from env or ~/.hermes/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.hermes/field-notes), ~/.hermes/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.hermes/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.hermes/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no_agent cron job only when the user runs install_cron.py. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-gemini-live (community, maintained by skappafrost) Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to Hermes. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — hermes_task starts, hermes_tasks reads the call's task board, and hermes_task_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "Hermes needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI_API_KEY from the Hermes home's .env; delegated work runs as a Hermes run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api_server and API_SERVER_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted. This plugin requires env var(s): GEMINI_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-guide (community, maintained by iap) Read-only diagnostics for Hermes configuration: /hermes-doctor in-session and hermes guide in a terminal. Seven read-only health checks (config, mcp, skills, commands, hooks, plugins, memories) and points to 20 troubleshooting skills, installed separately as a skills tap, for what the built-in doctor doesn't cover. Complements — never replaces — hermes doctor. Disclosure — reads config.yaml, SKILL.md frontmatter, skill bundles, plugin manifests, the shell-hooks allowlist and the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md stores read-only (the report quotes short memory snippets); /hermes-doctor and hermes guide run hermes config path and hermes hooks doctor as subprocesses (argument list, no shell), and hermes hooks doctor executes every approved shell hook once with a synthetic payload; with opt-in proactive: true it runs the checks in-process at each session start/end (no hooks executed) and once per process runs git ls-remote against the plugin's GitHub repo to log a newer-release notice (no download, no local writes). The 20 troubleshooting skills are not loaded by the plugin: they install separately from the repo as a skills tap, which this entry's pin does not cover. This plugin hook(s): on_session_start (opt-in proactive mode), on_session_end (opt-in proactive mode). Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-herald (community, maintained by bennybuoy) Cross-profile agent dispatch for Hermes Agent — 12 tools for agents talking to agents: async dispatch with SSE completion, synchronous multi-turn chat, model-selectable in-process subagents, a durable SQLite run ledger, fail-closed per-target model-route discovery, and host-owned bare LLM inference. Disclosure — sends task text and bearer tokens to the Hermes API servers you configure (plaintext HTTP permitted, warn-only); stores full dispatch text in a local SQLite ledger; delegate_subagent may use any provider credential you have configured. This plugin registers tool(s): dispatch_agent, check_dispatch, collect_dispatches, dispatch_status, dispatch_chat, cancel_dispatch, delegate_subagent, llm_call, llm_direct, ping_profile, approve_dispatch, list_profile_models. Requires Hermes >=0.21.0.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-honcho-plugin (community, maintained by outpoints) Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, and add confirmed corrections or source files. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through Hermes's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-insight (community, maintained by BrokeSkill) Selection-definition lookup for Hermes Desktop. Select any text, get an AI definition with sources in a popup. Renders the definition inline, runnable code aside. Backend is a stateless hermes insight CLI; panel, providers, and one-click model picking are configurable. Disclosure — definitions are generated with your configured provider keys (the selected term, your format template and optional web-search results are sent to that provider) via a short-lived `hermes insight` CLI run; no background process remains. When web search is on it also queries your configured searxng instance and fetches result thumbnails from their image hosts, inlining them into the panel; nothing is fetched without a searxng URL. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos, windows.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-iroh-interconnect (community, maintained by Richard Ahlquist) Authenticated Hermes agent-to-agent tasks and optional file transfer over Iroh QUIC. Disclosure — tasks from a paired peer run in your live gateway agent with its full toolset; pairing is confirmed via the tool's confirm=true argument, not a UI prompt. Uses n0's public relays by default (HERMES_IROH_RELAY=off or a self-hosted URL for LAN-only). iroh_send_file can share any readable path the model names (credential-name denylist only, overridable with allow_sensitive); remote-triggered auto-fetch is off by default and confined to HERMES_IROH_AUTO_FETCH_DIR. The Rust sidecar is built locally with cargo, never downloaded. This plugin registers tool(s): iroh_peer_status, iroh_peer_list, iroh_peer_pair, iroh_peer_make_ticket, iroh_send_file, iroh_fetch_file, iroh_transfer_status, iroh_peer_call, iroh_peer_settings. Platforms: linux, macos.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-jailbreak-kernel (community, maintained by Enchanted0911) Jailbreak-kernel plugin for Hermes Agent (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): session-scoped modes (off/slim/on/full) with kernel profiles (core/research/creative/max), session-aware system-prompt sections, llm_request request-layer system rebuild, and opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships a /jailbreak command, a progressive-disclosure ops skill, and a 276-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm_request middleware that, by default (`on`/`full` modes), replaces the system prompt on every request with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel plus only the memory and runtime-environment sections (agent rules, skills index, context files and other plugins' sections are dropped); `slim` appends it instead, and `off` passes requests through but strips all plugin prompt sections, including other plugins'. Rotates the x-opencode-session header on opencode routes. Writes a diagnostic dump per session (full system prompt incl. memory/persona text, plus the first 200 chars of every other message and the model/provider/base_url) to its own plugin dir (dumps/); `/jailbreak dump off` or `HERMES_JAILBREAK_DUMP=0` turns it off. No network, no exec. This plugin middleware: llm_request. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-kame-api-rotation (community, maintained by Kame696) Smart API key rotation: the healthiest key for every call, each 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / quota refusal sized from its own evidence. Install with its companion hermes-kame-provider, which hands Hermes this plugin's rotating client through ProviderProfile.create_client (and create_messages_client where Hermes offers it); no core override. Disclosure — /kame-keys add|import|split, and on start a key variable holding several comma-joined keys, write one auth.json pool row per key through Hermes' pool API after a plaintext backup (last 5 kept; switch: resolver_disabled); key-redacted, size-capped owner-only local logs and a status file per profile; the Desktop panel reads that file and queues its settings requests through its own dashboard/plugin_api.py route (GET /state, POST /control, this plugin's plugin-data folder only); while every key is resting, chats (CLI, Desktop, messaging gateway) keep waiting with no total limit (each key's rest capped by max_hold_seconds) and cron runs give up after 300 s with the provider's refusal unless max_total_wait_seconds is set. This plugin hook(s): transform_api_error_classification, post_api_request, on_session_reset. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-lcm-x (community, maintained by electricsheephq) Lossless context memory engine: instead of lossy compaction, LCM-X keeps every turn in a local SQLite store (lcm.db) and builds a recoverable DAG of summaries over it, with 15 lcm_* tools to search, recall and expand earlier context. Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from hermes-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Hermes, then in plugins.enabled replace hermes-lcm with hermes-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Hermes is configured with. Disclosure — optional semantic recall (embeddings_enabled, off by default) sends message text to the embedding provider you configure (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama); for known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in). The engine also reads Hermes' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Hermes builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use. This plugin registers tool(s): lcm_grep, lcm_recall, lcm_query_state, lcm_compute, lcm_compile_evidence, lcm_evidence_pack, lcm_retrieve, lcm_recent, lcm_load_session, lcm_describe, lcm_expand, lcm_expand_query, lcm_status, lcm_inspect, lcm_doctor; hook(s): pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, subagent_start, subagent_stop. Requires Hermes >=0.21.3.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-live-voice (community, maintained by Synero) Full-duplex Live Voice for Hermes Desktop — GPT-Live-1 on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription via the local Codex app-server, with live transcript, voice tool calls and task delegation to the user chat. Disclosure — subscription voice uses your Hermes openai-codex sign-in through Hermes-signed requests (requires_auth; the plugin never holds or refreshes the token) to mint OpenAI Realtime client secrets, and the usage panel reads Hermes's own account-usage fetcher; the gpt-live-1 lane runs the local codex app-server on the Codex CLI's own login, and the dashboard can run codex login --device-auth, copying ~/.codex/auth.json (or $CODEX_HOME) to a backup before that login, restoring the backup if the login is cancelled, and reading the file read-only for sign-in status; with TALK_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY set it uses that key instead; if hermes-talk is installed it loads that plugin's modules from ~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-talk and substitutes its own talk_auth; voice audio goes to OpenAI over WebRTC, and spoken tasks are submitted as messages in your focused chat. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-monitor (community, maintained by Hermes Monitor contributors (independent of Nous Research)) Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout (the related ai-usage-tracker plugin covers quota windows as a standalone feature). Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it reads every Hermes profile's credential pool (each profile's auth.json, with that profile's .env as secret scope) into read-only snapshots plus DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the environment or .env files, and calls Hermes' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch_account_usage), sending each entry's own token only to its own provider. The plugin never refreshes or persists a credential; on a Codex HTTP 401, Hermes core may refresh the active profile's matching Codex token via OpenAI's token endpoint and rewrite that profile's auth.json. No other network egress. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-teammates (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) Named subagent teammates for Hermes: the operator defines a roster (instructions, toolsets, model), and the agent assigns them work, checks results, steers a running teammate, follows up with a digest of earlier results, and can work a Kanban teammates lane with a review handoff. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock Hermes; no patched core. Disclosure — adds five tools and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process Hermes subagents on the parent's provider credentials; toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch), and a teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering dispatches delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent, so under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries; no transcripts or credentials). For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. It runs one in-process monitor thread per lane run to keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. This plugin registers tool(s): teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_check, teammate_message, teammate_stop. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary:
hermes-tenuo (community, maintained by tenuo-ai) Security guardrails for Hermes tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — hermes-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $HERMES_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, on_session_start, on_session_end, subagent_start; requires env var(s): TENUO_WARRANT, TENUO_SIGNING_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.20.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-verifier (community, maintained by am423) Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your Hermes session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read_file, search_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in HERMES_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read_file/search_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the process environment or the host `hermes` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to Hermes's stored credentials. This plugin hook(s): post_llm_call, pre_tool_call, pre_llm_call, pre_verify, on_session_reset. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-vision-inline (community, maintained by BrokeSkill) Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on Hermes private vision helpers, so after a Hermes update it may silently fall back to the normal path. This plugin middleware: tool_execution. Platforms: windows, macos, linux.

entries.capability_summary: hermes-workflows (community, maintained by jacobhausler) Agent-owned workflow graphs for Hermes — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock Hermes; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop; each agent node is a child hermes chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside Hermes' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $HERMES_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through Hermes' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml and POSTs a wake turn to the local Hermes API server — the gate.held wake only relays the gate to the human, but the run.done wake tells the woken session to turn the run's findings into tracked work and dispatch follow-up work (as PRs) before the turn ends, and the run.failed wake to apply one corrective amend/repair/resume; a transform_llm_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW_MAX_SEATS (that key only) from $HERMES_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; state lives under $HERMES_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No other network of its own. This plugin registers tool(s): workflow; hook(s): transform_llm_output. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: hicortex (community, maintained by gamaze-labs) Shared fleet memory for Hermes agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation. This plugin registers tool(s): hicortex_search, hicortex_get, hicortex_recent, hicortex_ingest, hicortex_lessons, hicortex_index, hicortex_graph, hicortex_update, hicortex_delete; requires env var(s): HICORTEX_URL, HICORTEX_AUTH_TOKEN.

entries.capability_summary: holographic (community, maintained by itpartypattaya) Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless the optional search by meaning (embeddings: on, off by default) is switched on. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.hermes-memory-store) and memory_store.db, so `hermes update` moves existing users onto it; the schema change is additive and older versions keep working on the file. Taken over from Nous Research's handoff copy (NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, hermes_home, mirror metadata, backup_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as_of a date) and `forget` erases a fact with all its versions from the file. Disclosure — local only unless the optional search by meaning is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db unless db_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact_store / fact_feedback calls do unless cron_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry, and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on (off by default): then the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Word forms are matched by stems, not a dictionary: an irregular form can miss (ponies / pony). A synonym is found only if the fact's keywords name it, unless the optional online search by meaning is on; facts stored without keywords (older ones, auto_extract) need `enrich`.; Arabic, Indic scripts, Indonesian, German, Turkish, Polish and Dutch are matched by scanning the facts' text: the first such search after start analyses every fact (about 1-1.5 s at 5,000 facts, 4-6 s at 20,000); stores without such facts never scan. The bundled dictionaries load on the first word of their language (Chinese about 0.2 s and 30 MB).; forget cleans the database file only: Hermes session history, `hermes backup` archives and copies other tools made are not rewritten (tools can read the `forgotten` table and clean their own copies by fact id)..

entries.capability_summary: honcho (community, maintained by plastic-labs) Honcho is memory infrastructure for building stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects, and ideas over time. Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework. Use it managed at api.honcho.dev, run a local stack with the honcho CLI, or self-host the server yourself. Maintained by Plastic Labs; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns, derived conclusions and peer/session ids are sent to the Honcho API (api.honcho.dev by default, or the self-hosted base_url you configure) under your HONCHO_API_KEY; every request also carries X-Honcho-Host (Hermes version and OS platform) and X-Honcho-Plugin (plugin version) headers that Honcho records for usage attribution. This plugin hook(s): on_session_end; requires env var(s): HONCHO_API_KEY.

entries.capability_summary: huddo (community, maintained by puffo-ai) Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, react, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.9.0, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, and Hermes does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skill tells the agent to get confirmation in your own Hermes chat before anything sensitive. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars.

entries.capability_summary: hwiki (community, maintained by ottosulin) Markdown wiki as Hermes long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside HERMES_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Hermes's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at HERMES_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in HERMES_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to hermes backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB). This plugin registers tool(s): wiki_memory_search, wiki_memory_read, wiki_memory_write, wiki_memory_status. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: hyatlas (community, maintained by tuancookiez-hub) HyAtlas v4 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories stay local. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `hermes hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings and stored memories stay local. Extraction is opt-in: the server has no default LLM endpoint and makes no LLM call until HYATLAS_LLM_BASE, HYATLAS_LLM_MODEL and HYATLAS_LLM_KEY are all set. The repo installer pre-fills a free Nous Portal endpoint that Enter accepts, but nothing is sent until you also enter a key. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters). In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions and recent summaries to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY). An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, Hermes starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `hermes hyatlas start` keeps running after Hermes exits until `hermes hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `hermes hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads your Nous token from Hermes auth.json and points extraction at the Nous Portal. No telemetry. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4. Known issues: After enabling, select the provider with `hermes memory setup` (memory.provider: hyatlas) — installing and enabling alone does not activate memory.; The agent tools and hooks arrive through the MemoryProvider interface, not ctx.register_tool, so they do not appear in the plugin tool list.; Requires the separate hyatlas-go server binary (installed by the user); without a reachable server the provider reports unavailable and memory features degrade rather than fail.; Updating the plugin does not update the server: install hyatlas-go v4.7.3 too. A store written by an earlier version can be cleaned with the server's maintenance endpoints (see after-install.md, 'Upgrading a store written before 4.5.0')..

entries.capability_summary:
index-network (community, maintained by indexnetwork) Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `hermes index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the Hermes env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Hermes model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $HERMES_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Hermes env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Hermes sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled. This plugin registers tool(s): index_read_intents, index_research_profile, index_create_intent, index_update_intent, index_add_intent_to_network, index_list_intent_networks, index_read_networks, index_read_network_memberships, index_update_network, index_create_network, index_join_network, index_list_opportunities, index_update_opportunity, index_read_docs, index_agent_me, index_open_app; requires env var(s): INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN.

entries.capability_summary: index-search (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can search with your key and approve a watch. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. index_watch schedule creates one cron job that runs a model turn every 15 minutes (two or more model requests when it calls the tool) with no daily cap, and it watches only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Scheduling and unscheduling ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, where the watch only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. This plugin registers tool(s): index_search, index_health, index_watch; requires env var(s): MEILI_HOST, MEILI_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: invinoveritas-receipts (community, maintained by babyblueviper1) Signed, independently checkable receipts for Hermes approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Hermes passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl. This plugin hook(s): post_approval_response, post_llm_call, on_session_end; requires env var(s): INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY.

The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Not tested from a Hermes model. This plugin registers tool(s): address_split. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: jp-edinet (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with hermes tools. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in Hermes. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false only means the figure is missing from the consolidated current-year rows the plugin reads, not that the document has no number. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on Hermes internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup. This plugin registers tool(s): edinet_search_filings, edinet_financials, edinet_save_document; requires env var(s): EDINET_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: jp-egov-law (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Japanese laws for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, Hermes tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until hermes cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint. This plugin registers tool(s): egov_law_search, egov_law_article, egov_law_revisions. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: jp-kokkai (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Posts new Diet meeting hits as metadata and the official meeting URL, with kokkai_search and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key, and never requests or stores speech text. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, add a watch and approve it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. kokkai_watch add creates one cron job that runs a model turn once a day, at the hour you pick in Hermes's own timezone, with no daily cap. It stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch asks for Hermes approval every time and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot save seen speech IDs and says so on every run. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. Each request waits up to 30 seconds for data, and a whole run has no time limit. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall. Tested with a stand-in server on Hermes 0.21.4 and current main, not in a live chat. This plugin registers tool(s): kokkai_search, kokkai_watch. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: jp-subsidies (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with hermes tools. The /subsidies command is outside hermes tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run hermes cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows. This plugin registers tool(s): subsidies_search, subsidies_detail, subsidies_watch_setup. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: kanban-gantt (community, maintained by e-is) Gantt timeline view for the Hermes kanban boards: a full /kanban-gantt desktop page rendering any board as a timeline of real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), an optional List view beside the timeline (task, assignee, status, last activity — the timeline stays the default), task creation (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parenting by drag & drop or from the drawer, live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a dockable task detail drawer. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: kanban-task-threads (community, maintained by diegomarino) Give every Hermes kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels). This plugin hook(s): kanban_task_claimed, kanban_task_completed, kanban_task_blocked, on_kanban_task_updated, on_kanban_worker_spawned, on_kanban_worker_exited, on_kanban_worker_stale_claim, on_kanban_dispatch_tick; requires env var(s): KANBAN_TASK_THREADS_WEBHOOK_URL. Requires Hermes >=0.20.
