entries.capability_summary: kfchow-llm-value-router (community, maintained by KFChow) Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.hermes/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.hermes/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated. This plugin middleware: llm_request, llm_execution. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: kimchi-acp-provider (community, maintained by getkimchi) The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Hermes model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Hermes's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Hermes cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Hermes. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: letsfg (community, maintained by LetsFG) Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and Hermes itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Known issues: Sign-in needs one extra command after install, because a portable mcp.json cannot declare OAuth: hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300.

entries.capability_summary: limbic (community, maintained by dyiapanis) Self-organising memory provider (MemoryProvider ABC): local SQLite (WAL) with sqlite-vec KNN + FTS5 hybrid recall, adaptive trust scoring, activation maturation, interference-based forgetting, NLI-based correction detection and synaptic atrophy. No LLM cost — all lifecycle mechanisms are deterministic. The optional inline chat recall indicator is off by default (recall_indicator in limbic.yaml) and memory injection works identically either way. Recall is confidence-gated: when nothing clears the calibration floor, recall abstains (no_confident_match) instead of surfacing near-misses, and the agent answers from what it knows without attributing anything to memory. Tools (remember/recall) and lifecycle hooks dispatch via the MemoryManager from the registered provider — this entry registers a MemoryProvider only, so provides_tools/provides_hooks are empty. Disclosure — on first primary session start downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB, on first contradiction check) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside HERMES_HOME); at every model load, every file in those cache folders that is not in the pinned manifest is deleted — including unrelated files if you point embedding/nli cache_dir at a shared folder — which reclaims stale orphans from prior versions (e.g. an older fp32 cache of ~2.2GB); the memory database is never touched; spaCy NER models are not downloaded and must be installed manually for entity extraction; memory stays local in limbic.db under HERMES_HOME, and hermes backup adds VACUUM snapshots under HERMES_HOME/backups; no telemetry. Stores created or reindexed on 0.6.0+ record the embedder that produced their vectors and report stale_embedder=true after an embedder change until `hermes limbic reindex`; stores from 0.5.x keep serving their fp32 vectors unflagged until reindexed. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license). This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

A top-level `reasoning_effort` is sent only when you select a level. This plugin requires env var(s): LIQUID_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: llm-antidote (community, maintained by GroveMinting) Runtime guardrails, behavioral evaluation, and signed fleet admission for Hermes Agent: a versioned capability policy that blocks or requires approval for model tool calls, paired synthetic behavioral evaluation with no real side effects, and a signed local promotion gate that refuses a model whose evidence does not satisfy signed fleet policy. Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to Hermes's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. The user-run `hermes antidote eval run` command sends synthetic prompts (and the API key you name) to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you pass, as billed model calls (default suite up to ~170 requests); `model inspect hf:` queries huggingface.co; `fleet keygen` writes unencrypted Ed25519 private keys (mode 0600) to paths you choose. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_api_request, on_session_start, on_session_reset, on_session_finalize. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: local-system-one-hermes (community, maintained by NMTZ-z) Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Hermes Agent. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model. This plugin hook(s): pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, on_session_end; middleware: llm_request. Platforms: macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: lowrouter (community, maintained by carboniferio) LowRouter as a Hermes model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `hermes model`). The picker shows the 180 `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of all 719 IDs from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of Hermes' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and Hermes shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through Hermes' open_credentialed_url. No files read or written, no processes. This plugin requires env var(s): LOWROUTER_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: lumberroom (community, maintained by lumberroom) lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.3.

entries.capability_summary: max-platform (community, maintained by Realmagnum) MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under HERMES_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Hermes pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update. This plugin hook(s): transform_llm_output; requires env var(s): MAX_BOT_TOKEN. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active Hermes profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret. This plugin requires env var(s): MEMORIA_API_KEY. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Development preview: local CLI acceptance passed; Desktop has not been validated and gateway platforms are disabled.; Auto capture is off by default. One-shot CLI exit can interrupt an in-flight capture, leaving an uncertain event requiring manual inspection.; Explicit-write exclusions apply to the current turn only. Auto capture can retain paraphrases, recalled facts from later turns, transient results or operation requests; global semantic deduplication is not guaranteed.; Ambiguous write outcomes are not automatically retried; this plugin does not provide exactly-once capture..

entries.capability_summary: memory-shield (community, maintained by churnast) Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Hermes' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Hermes' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is Hermes' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Hermes' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Needs plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under plugins.isolation: host the plugin cannot see the current chat, sender or Hermes' review marker, so it judges every call like a direct chat and the group chat and background review protection does not apply.; Covers Hermes' built-in memory tool (USER.md, MEMORY.md) only, not the tools of memory provider plugins such as Honcho or Mem0.; Without trusted_users every direct chat counts as the owner: whoever can message the agent directly may add facts to the owner profile and correct them (not delete them) until the owner's id is listed.; Spotting USER.md and MEMORY.md edits made through terminal and execute_code is best effort: a path built some other way, or a command run from a script file, can get through.; terminal and execute_code calls are read up to 16,384 characters. A longer call that contains the word memories, USER.md or MEMORY.md (any case, quotes ignored) is refused even when it only reads them; a longer call that contains none of them passes without being read..

entries.capability_summary: memtomem (community, maintained by memtomem) Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.8) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside Hermes's MCP environment filtering. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "hermes auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the Hermes credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely. This plugin requires env var(s): MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY.

entries.capability_summary: model-router (community, maintained by metamindedu) Profile model settings, opt-in Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads Hermes profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background Hermes children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — once you enable routing for a profile, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background Hermes agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs. This plugin registers tool(s): coding_route; hook(s): pre_api_request, post_api_request, api_request_error, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, subagent_start, subagent_stop; middleware: tool_execution, llm_request. Platforms: windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: Preferences now live under Settings > Plugins. The main-sidebar settings row is removed; legacy /model-router bookmarks remain supported. A host supporting the public plugin-settings area is needed; no private-core or sidebar fallback is added.; The Desktop UI is Korean-first. Windows runtime/SDK/Desktop behavior has been tested; full Linux/macOS runtime support is not claimed.; Requires a Hermes build with unified Python/Desktop packages and request/tool middleware; new Python tools may require a new session.; Fast and fallback can increase API charges or subscription-credit use. Transports bypassing the request middleware, including codex_app_server, are outside Fast inheritance coverage.; The native scanner can report CAUTION for the manual source-repair helper; routing-disabled capability probes can warn that coding_route was not registered.; Default-profile mid-run activation was not confirmed on the developer's shared backend; package installation is distinct from existing-session activation..

Fast and fallback can increase API charges or subscription-credit use. Transports bypassing the request middleware, including codex_app_server, are outside Fast inheritance coverage.

entries.capability_summary: nexus (community, maintained by Neboy72) Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant with automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget/guardrail tools and a knowledge graph. Embeddings run locally by default: sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (1024d, about 1.2 GB downloaded from Hugging Face on first use), no key and no extra software needed. Ollama is used only when it is chosen explicitly, and a cloud embedder (Voyage, OpenAI, Google, Jina) only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it together with its key. A key that merely sits in the environment does NOT select a provider on its own, and there is no silent cloud fallback. Query rewriting plus paid consolidation stations stay off until enabled. Hermes and any MCP-connected agent share one collection, so they read and write the same memories. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level is treated as the most restrictive one, so a missing value never looks like permission. The local service that serves embeddings on 127.0.0.1:9122 demands a per-installation key for its /embed and /mcp routes (generated once, stored under the data directory as service_auth.key with mode 0600, sent by the plugin) and rejects requests whose Host or Origin is not loopback; the open /healthz answers liveness only. Disclosure — when Hermes's environment cannot load the embedding stack, the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings plus the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon whose default Ollama model `glm-5.3-flash:cloud` can send memory text to Ollama's cloud), and the service keeps running after Hermes exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Hermes config.yaml; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; an opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt. This plugin registers tool(s): nexus_recall, nexus_remember, nexus_forget, nexus_guardrail_check, nexus_guardrail_override, nexus_graph_traverse, nexus_find_entities, nexus_get_subgraph, nexus_get_related, nexus_cost_routing_stats, nexus_cost_routing_explain, nexus_sica_run; hook(s): transform_llm_output. Requires Hermes >=0.19.

entries.capability_summary: openltm (community, maintained by RohiRIK) Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. entries.capability_summary: operations (community, maintained by c-pompa) A Hermes Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads hermes-metrics-dash's <hermes root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <hermes root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through hermes send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task. This plugin hook(s): on_kanban_dispatch_tick. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. entries.capability_summary: orbit-desktop (community, maintained by mojomast) Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research. This plugin registers tool(s): orbit_workspace. Platforms: linux.

entries.capability_summary: orcaslicer (community, maintained by mazzanfar) Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. entries.capability_summary: pass-secrets (community, maintained by dyiapanis) pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Stdlib-only (subprocess + pathlib), no Python deps, no network — ever. Config: secrets.pass.{enabled,store_path,subdirs,override_existing,timeout_seconds}. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: pdf-surgeon (community, maintained by Samuek9) Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Hermes installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from. This plugin registers tool(s): pdf_replace_text. Platforms: linux, macos, windows.

entries.capability_summary: plan-mode (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) Claude Code-style plan mode on every interactive Hermes surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent submits the plan with plan_mode(submit) and you approve it through Hermes' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve); it then implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress. Deny keeps planning and the agent revises. When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks one clarify question instead (Approve plan rev N / Keep planning), and only that answer approves. By default plans are compact and decision-complete and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, allow_commits and plan_skill settings; plan_style: core keeps the zero-context /plan craft). The default lean profile keeps compact planning short: a brief planning note, at most three targeted questions, and no todo bookkeeping for short plans (plan_profile: classic keeps 0.3.5); on TUI, Desktop and hermes serve the agent writes the plan once, in its reply, and the plugin saves it. Classic CLI enforced on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. It reads eight groups of internal Hermes seams for session identity, workspace, profile and skills.inline_shell, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .hermes/plans under the session working directory and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When you pick "Always" on a plan approval, Hermes core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and hermes serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file. No network calls, no subprocesses, no self-updater. This plugin registers tool(s): plan_mode; hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call, transform_llm_output, pre_approval_request, post_approval_response, on_session_finalize, on_session_reset, post_llm_call, transform_tool_result, post_api_request. Requires Hermes >=0.21.3.
entries.description: Claude Code-style plan mode on every interactive Hermes surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent submits the plan with plan_mode(submit) and you approve it through Hermes' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve); it then implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress. Deny keeps planning and the agent revises. When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks one clarify question instead (Approve plan rev N / Keep planning), and only that answer approves. By default plans are compact and decision-complete and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, allow_commits and plan_skill settings; plan_style: core keeps the zero-context /plan craft). The default lean profile keeps compact planning short: a brief planning note, at most three targeted questions, and no todo bookkeeping for short plans (plan_profile: classic keeps 0.3.5); on TUI, Desktop and hermes serve the agent writes the plan once, in its reply, and the plugin saves it. Classic CLI enforced on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. It reads eight groups of internal Hermes seams for session identity, workspace, profile and skills.inline_shell, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .hermes/plans under the session working directory and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When you pick "Always" on a plan approval, Hermes core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and hermes serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file. No network calls, no subprocesses, no self-updater.

entries.title: Plan mode

entries.capability_summary: print-job-watch (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, and when those checks cannot run. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running hermes tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" adds one unused line to config.yaml, and that line does not approve the next move. The optional watch is a cron job you create from the CLI (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. The watch needs plugins.isolation: in_process; under host it only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam. This plugin registers tool(s): print_job_status, print_job_control, print_job_watch; requires env var(s): OCTOPRINT_URL, OCTOPRINT_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account (fails closed); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions; sends session events with a hashed hostname on every turn, redacted tool-error text (max 3 per session) and redacted gated-tool arguments to pushary.com.

entries.capability_summary: pushover-hermes-plugin (community, maintained by lightx) Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, Hermes's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands, the command waiting on the sudo password prompt (redacted by Hermes; never the password) and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $HERMES_HOME/logs and settings.json under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data, and $HERMES_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. This plugin hook(s): post_llm_call, pre_approval_request, post_approval_response, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, on_human_input_request; requires env var(s): PUSHOVER_APP_TOKEN, PUSHOVER_USER_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: qdrant-memory (community, maintained by cnkang) Durable native memory for Hermes with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the Hermes-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update and qdrant_memory_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and `migrate mem0` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — memory text is stored in the configured Qdrant store (embedded files under <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory/qdrant by default, or the Server/Cloud URL you set), and memory text plus each turn's recall query are sent as plain text to the configured embedding endpoint (default local Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434; an OpenAI-compatible remote endpoint can be configured, and keyed endpoints must use HTTPS). Disclosure — after each primary-agent turn, at session end and before context compression, conversation text goes to the LLM configured in Hermes through the Hermes plugin LLM facade (a provider/model override needs the plugin's Hermes trust grant) to extract facts and to compare near-duplicate memories; that LLM may be a remote provider. Disclosure — the provider is selected with memory.provider: qdrant-memory; its settings live in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory.json (0600, secrets stripped on save). QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_API_KEY are read through the Hermes secret scope, but an api_key written by hand into qdrant-memory.json takes precedence, and `migrate mem0` reads the source Qdrant endpoint and any api_key from <HERMES_HOME>/mem0.json or --source-config. Disclosure — state lives under <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory/ (embedded store, SQLite WAL ledger, lock files); the ledger holds raw turn text and pre-compression transcripts until they are processed, and failed items until retried, then scrubs the bodies. Disclosure — single-writer design: a local ownership lock excludes a second writer to the same profile destination, and Server/Cloud deployments expect one active writer per scope. Disclosure — deletion removes records and fences pending operations, but is not a forensic secure erase (SQLite WAL pages and backups may retain content). This plugin registers tool(s): qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update, qdrant_memory_delete. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Preview scope: multi-writer Server/Cloud deployments, hybrid retrieval and a web UI are not supported.; Deletion removes records and fences pending operations but is not a forensic secure erase; storage-level remnants (WAL, backups) may persist.; Embedded mode is single-writer: a second process fails closed on the ownership lock instead of sharing the store.; Extraction adds LLM latency after a turn; memory admission is not guaranteed before the host admits the provider, and pending operations replay on the next start..

entries.capability_summary: qdrant (community, maintained by kuehnberger) Dense semantic memory for Hermes, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off | summary | verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off | minimal | verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Hermes secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-status.json. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.hermes/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/hermes_default, ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base Hermes home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate hermes_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Hermes process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's Hermes session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it. This plugin registers tool(s): qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget, md_search. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Windows on ARM is unsupported: grpcio, pulled in by qdrant-client, has no win_arm64 wheel. Linux and macOS on x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 are supported.; Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported — the provider is REST-only and requires a reachable server.; md_search returns 'no markdown index yet' until you run the bundled ingest script once (python scripts/md_ingest.py, lexical only and fast; add --semantic for the embedding tier, which takes about 7 minutes for 5500 chunks on a 5-core CPU). No background process does this for you.; Running the plugin's pytest suite inside an installed copy still changes the PM dependency stamp (the .pytest_cache directory is hashed as a build input); only an upstream core change can exclude gitignored state..

entries.capability_summary: quota (community, maintained by rarf) Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the hermes-quota-plugin User-Agent; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from Hermes' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, Hermes' auth.json pool and OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check reads local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux or the macOS Keychain for the browser's Safe Storage key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or Hermes' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA_API_KEY from ~/.hermes/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from Hermes' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints. This plugin hook(s): footer, usage_extra.

entries.capability_summary: quotum (community, maintained by quotum) A quotum seat's Venice key as a provider. Private and anonymized models, with the seat's daily cap, spend and the 20:00 UTC bell in /usage, and a Seals tab in hermes dashboard with the seat's record. Disclosure — prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY go to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage and the Seals tab send a 16-hex sha256 handle of the key to quotum.org, then the Seals tab reads the seat's public record from quotum.org (the key itself is never sent there); QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 swaps in its own client that drops Hermes web_search for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token This plugin requires env var(s): QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: The optional QUOTUM_X_SEARCH mode supplies its own client through create_client, so it works with plugins.isolation in_process (the default) only; under host isolation leave it off.; Hermes' bundled Achievements page has no hook for outside achievements, so the seat's seals live in the plugin's own Seals tab..

entries.capability_summary: radio-dm-gateway (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC_ALLOWED_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until hermes tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until hermes cron remove. Hermes main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project. This plugin requires env var(s): MESHTASTIC_URL. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: rea (official, maintained by NousResearch) Reverse engineer programs with REA (rea.tools): native binaries, .NET assemblies, Electron/JavaScript apps, Android packages, firmware and browser/process activity, through REA's MCP server (pinned rea-agents@6.4.0 over npx stdio) with REA's reverse-engineer-anything skill adapted for Hermes. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ on PATH, plus your own Ghidra, Hopper or IDA for native decompilation. Disclosure — a few REA tools run a command under a PTY, launch or drive an application, change a connected Android device or overwrite a chosen file, and Hermes does not prompt before them; the bundled skill tells the agent to ask first and to skip them in unattended runs. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.22.0.

entries.capability_summary: secure-env-ingress (community, maintained by web3blind) One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, protected hosted payment-field filling, nested HTTPS verification codes/passcodes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Explicit parent payment/nested-code targeting requires compatible host task/profile ownership and browser-generation evidence and fails closed without it; this is not a general fix for native Vault named-tab selection. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer. Disclosure — When you ask to connect, it adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by Hermes) to the profile's config.yaml, and Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform there. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass Hermes allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook blocks every tool except the Senler MCP and pins replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a Hermes approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<HERMES_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. This plugin registers tool(s): senler_connect; hook(s): pre_tool_call, on_session_end. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: Preview: Windows Desktop sign-in is confirmed; a real Senler Relay workflow still needs end-to-end verification.; Requires current Hermes with native MCP OAuth and Relay transport; gateway proxy mode and multiplexed profiles are unsupported..

entries.capability_summary: session-mirror (community, maintained by rrrrnmtsu) Mirrors Hermes Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after Hermes's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $HERMES_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `hermes session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread. This plugin hook(s): post_llm_call. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: skill-retrieval (community, maintained by moonlight-lupin) BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $HERMES_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files. This plugin hook(s): pre_llm_call, on_skill_lifecycle; middleware: llm_request. Requires Hermes >=0.21.1.

entries.capability_summary: tameru (community, maintained by 0xWhiteMage) Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_expand tool brings back the exact original. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Subclasses Hermes's built-in ContextCompressor and overrides its private prune/demote methods (checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens Hermes's re-prune runway. Adds a model-callable tameru_expand tool that returns pruned tool output from memory or from this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process. No network calls; the render log is off by default. This plugin registers tool(s): tameru_expand. Platforms: linux. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7. Known issues: Full archive recovery requires plugins.isolation to be in_process; host mode limits recovery.; Overrides private ContextCompressor signatures and falls back when the host contract changes..

entries.capability_summary: teamorouter (community, maintained by TeamoRouter) TeamoRouter as Hermes model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: hermes-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes. This plugin requires env var(s): TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: telegram-stickers (community, maintained by churnast) Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, read through Hermes' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender Hermes answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in Hermes. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max_learned_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn_packs: false turns learning off). A pre_llm_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads Hermes' sticker_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through Hermes like any tool. Uses Hermes functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision_tools.vision_analyze_tool, gateway.session_context.get_session_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only. This plugin registers tool(s): telegram_sticker_find, telegram_sticker_send, telegram_sticker_mute, telegram_sticker_settings; hook(s): pre_llm_call; requires env var(s): TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.20.6. Known issues: Needs plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under plugins.isolation: host it cannot see the current chat, so it sends no stickers, learns no packs and adds no hint.; Every person the bot answers in a direct chat adds packs (up to max_learned_packs, default 100), which the agent then uses in every chat. Keep the gateway allowlist to yourself, or set learn_packs: false.; Before Hermes 0.21.5, /stickers in Telegram only shows the status and reloads packs; the owner's other /stickers commands work in the Hermes CLI on the server.; Where tool progress is on, Hermes posts its progress line (such as telegram_sticker_send...) before a sticker; display.platforms.telegram.tool_progress: off hides every tool's lines in Telegram..

Before Hermes 0.21.5, /stickers in Telegram only shows the status and reloads packs; the owner's other /stickers commands work in the Hermes CLI on the server.
Where tool progress is on, Hermes posts its progress line (such as telegram_sticker_send...) before a sticker; display.platforms.telegram.tool_progress: off hides every tool's lines in Telegram.

entries.title: Telegram Stickers

entries.capability_summary: telegram_dashboard_probe (community, maintained by bablobanov) One pinned Telegram message with the state of your Hermes on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, whether the agent sees its rules and whether its memory writes stand unapproved, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from Hermes' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through Hermes' own auth code); at most once per limits_refresh_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes request to xAI, may refresh that OAuth token and save it to auth.json, or clear a dead one, through Hermes' own auth code), sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host Hermes itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes key lookup without a usable key in .env or the environment, may save Hermes' credential pool back to auth.json once when loading it changes something, e.g. a placeholder key in .env) and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a *_BOT_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of HERMES_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; with a memory provider configured, the last 256 KB of the same log are also read for the engine's warnings about that provider, of which only the time and whether one says unavailable are kept; every tick HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job_id, status, delivery_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send_path_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (_updates_received_total, _polling_generation, _polling_last_progress_monotonic, _polling_generation_started_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; every tick HERMES_HOME/state.db is opened read-only the same way for the newest saved system prompt of each platform the running gateway lists in HERMES_HOME/gateway_state.json, and the project context files the engine would load (.hermes.md or HERMES.md in that directory and each parent up to the git root, the AGENTS.override.md / AGENTS.md / agents.md chain from the git root down, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc; up to 4 MB each, links followed as the engine follows them) are read from the directory that prompt names (else the engine's TERMINAL_CWD or the gateway's working directory), and .hermes.md, HERMES.md and the AGENTS names also from the gateway's working directory and HERMES_HOME, which may be outside HERMES_HOME; to tell whether the prompt carries them as they are on disk; only a verdict, the file names, sizes and times are kept, never the prompt's or a file's text; every tick HERMES_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (up to 4 MB each) are read to count their characters against the limits, the waiting writes in HERMES_HOME/pending/memory and pending/skills (up to 2,000 files) for their names and times and, of the memory ones (up to 256 KB each), each add's target and length, and the time of HERMES_HOME/skills/.curator_ledger.jsonl; never a notebook's, an entry's or a waiting write's text, and nothing there is written; the private hermes_cli.version_info._cached_version_info and the signature of agent.prompt_builder._read_text_with_timeout are read from modules the gateway already imported, and nothing is called or changed on them; the release check keeps only each release's version and publication time and downloads, installs or replaces nothing; config.yaml is read through Hermes' own YAML parser for the memory limits, switches, approval gate and provider name, skills.write_approval and each platform's skip_context_files; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (Hermes' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest Hermes release is read from api.github.com without a token at most once per 15 minutes (releases/latest with the last answer's ETag; the release list releases?per_page=100 only when Latest names another version); an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.1. Known issues: Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram handler factory receives the platform's native SDK client, which plugins.isolation: host does not allow; under host the plugin does not load and nothing is delivered..

entries.capability_summary: thomas (community, maintained by keppy) Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Hermes venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under HERMES_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies. This plugin registers tool(s): thomas_check_data, thomas_encoder_train, thomas_run_status, thomas_encoder_eval; hook(s): pre_tool_call. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: tinyfish (community, maintained by tinyfish-io) First-party TinyFish plugin: free Search and Fetch as a web provider, plus credit-gated remote Browser sessions and the tinyfish_agent web agent. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through Hermes's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `hermes tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to Hermes .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking. This plugin registers tool(s): tinyfish_agent; hook(s): pre_tool_call, pre_llm_call, on_session_finalize; requires env var(s): TINYFISH_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.19.

entries.capability_summary: ttsbuddy (community, maintained by ngelik) Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Hermes voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `hermes ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin. This plugin registers tool(s): ttsbuddy_recover. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7. Known issues: Account deletion is terminal-only, requires CLI 0.16.0+ and an explicit persistent cli_config_dir; speech credentials do not authorize deletion.; Use fresh unique output filenames/stems: successful Hermes delivery and same-stem Opus conversion can replace files outside the provider's no-clobber checks.; MP3 source audio only; no PCM streaming. A local timeout does not cancel an accepted hosted job; use ttsbuddy_recover with the exact job ID..

entries.capability_summary: unbrowse (community, maintained by unbrowse-ai) Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. entries.capability_summary: unitares (community, maintained by cirwel) Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only. This plugin hook(s): on_session_finalize, on_session_reset, on_session_start, post_llm_call, pre_llm_call; requires env var(s): UNITARES_MCP_URL. Requires Hermes >=0.21.0.
